newsitem.title: USA: U.S. help-wanted ad index fell to 81 in May.
newsitem.headline: U.S. help-wanted ad index fell to 81 in May.

text.p: The Conference Board's U.S. help-wanted advertising index fell six points in May, declining to 81.0 versus a revised 87.0 in April, the Conference Board said on Thursday.
The index read 79.0 a year ago.

In the last three months, help-wanted advertising volume fell in all nine regions. The steepest declines were in the Middle Atlantic, off 20.8 percent; West North Central, off 13.0 percent; and South Atlantic, off 10.2 percent, the Conference Board said.
"This latest decline in job advertising is not necessarily a sign that the labor market is cooling down," Conference Board economist Ken Goldstein said.
"The index has been so fixed in a narrow range of about 85 to 90 in the last two years that this latest change may only be an abberation," he said.
Goldstein said that the current high level of consumer optimism will sustain consumption increases, and raise inventory demand and industrial growth.

"A faster rise in industrial growth could feed through all regions of the country and deliver a kind of economy where consumer confidence hits peaks not seen in three decades, and unemployment rates drop to levels not seen in more than four decades," Goldstein added.
The Conference Board surveys advertising volume in 51 major newspapers across the country each month.
